newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-ARGENTINA FINISH WITH EIGHT AS THEY LOSE TO PERU.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINA FINISH WITH EIGHT AS THEY LOSE TO PERU.

text.p: Argentina, in yet another display of bad temper, had three players sent off as they were dumped out of the Copa America in a 2-1 defeat by Peru Saturday.

Two were dismissed in a fight which began when Marcelo Gallardo, having converted a penalty for Argentina to make the score 2-1 in the quarter-final tie, rushed to fetch the ball from the net to get the game re-started quickly.
Peru goalkeeper Miguel Miranda got to the ball at the same time as Gallardo and the two began fighting for the ball, leading to a brawl involving most of the players on the field.

One Peruvian appeared to be punched in the face during the fight, which ended with Gallardo and Eduardo Berizzo being shown the red card. Gustavo Zapata was later sent off for a second bookable offence.
Eddie Carazas and Martin Hidalgo had earlier put Peru 2-0 ahead, setting them up for a deserved victory in which goalkeeper Miguel Miranda performed heroics.
It was the second successive game that Gallardo had missed one penalty and scored another.
Both teams had brought second-string outfits to the tournament, preferring to rest their top players for the World Cup qualifying matches.
Peru's young team made a lively start and missed a glorious chance early on when Roberto Palacios found himself with a clean run at goal but fired his shot against the post.
Miranda made two reflex saves with the score still at 0-0 before Eddie Carrazas fired Peru in front in the 30th minute after a mistake by the Argentine midfield.
Argentina's play was often shoddy as they misplaced numerous passes and coach Daniel Passarella made three halftime substitutions in a desperate attempt to bring some life to the team.
The changes seemed as if they would pay off as Argentina created a series of chances early in the second half.
However, Miranda saved everything Argentina could throw at him, including a weakly-hit penalty by Gallardo in the 49th minute.
Peru struck the killer blow in the 62nd minute when Martin Hidalgo scored with a low shot from the edge of the penalty area after an exquisite flicked pass by Palacios.

The game turned ugly when Argentina were awarded a hugely controversial penalty for handball in the 72nd minute. Sergio Berti's pass struck the hand of Jose Reyna, but there seemed no possible way Reyna could have got his hand out of the way in time. Gallardo this time scored but almost instantly got sent off in the melee that followed.
It was the second time in less than three months that Argentina have been involved in a tumultuous match in Bolivia.

In April, they had two players sent off as they lost 2-1 to Bolivia in a World Cup qualifier in La Paz. Near the end of the game, Argentina's players became involved in a brawl that held up play for ten minutes.

Argentina - 19-Carlos Roa, 21-Nelson Vivas, 22-Gustavo Zapata, 2-Eduardo Berizzo, 6-Raul Cardozo (13-Jorge Martinez, 46), 5-Rodolfo Cardozo (3-Sergio Berti, 46), 1-Christian Bassedas, 17-Mauricio Pineda, 8-Marcelo Delgado, 9-Marcelo Gallardo, 7-Julio Cruz (18-Martin Posse, 46).

Peru - 1-Miguel Miranda, 2-Jose Reyna, 3-Miguel Rebosio, 5-Alfonso Dulanto, 14-Martin Hidalgo, 6-Erick Torres, 7-German Munoz, 10-Roberto Palacios, 17-Eddie Carrazas (13-Orlando Prado, 50), 18-Waldir Saenz (20-Frank Palomina, 72), 9-Paul Cominges (15-Aldo Cavero, 75)
